clue.text: Clash of politicians after moving to centre

indicators.note: after places the politicians' letters behind the rearranged ones
moving the letters around means the words to centre are rearranged

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament, politicians

explanation.surface: A row breaks out among politicians after someone shifts towards the political centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' is the anagram signal, not a political shift; 'after' places the politicians last.
explanation.definitionFit: A contretemps is a minor dispute or awkward disagreement, so it is a clash.

clue.text: Old, not very bright, full of universal hatred

indicators.note: full of means the dim word holds the universal letter within it

parts.note: dim means not very bright, whether of light or intellect
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: An old, dim person is brimming with hatred for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts U inside DIM, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or disgust directed at someone, a synonym.

clue.text: Taught wine after time out for revision

indicators.note: after places the wine behind the reworked letters
revision here means reworking, so the letters of time and out are reordered

parts.note: red is a kind of wine

explanation.surface: Someone was taught about wine after taking time out to revise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for revision' suggests study but is the anagram signal on the second word; 'after' places the wine last.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor is to teach privately, so tutored means taught, a synonym.

clue.text: Artificial flowers at zebra crossing

indicators.note: crossing here means the answer spans the word boundaries of flowers at zebra

explanation.surface: Fake flowers have been left at a zebra crossing, perhaps as a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' signals the answer lying across flowERS AT Zebra. A zebra crossing is a British striped pedestrian crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior substitute or imitation, hence artificial.

clue.text: Imposed objective, binding for church

indicators.note: binding means the objective wraps around the other letters, tying them in

parts.note: an end is an objective or aim
CE is the Church of England abbreviation

explanation.surface: An objective was imposed, binding on the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding' reads as 'obligatory' but signals a container: the objective wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Enforced means compelled or imposed by authority, a synonym of imposed.

clue.text: In a wretched state, we're heard to demand sympathy

indicators.note: we're heard means this is what we say out loud, so it signals a sound-alike

parts.note: to demand sympathy we would cry the two-word plea 'pity us'

explanation.surface: People in a sorry state are making their plea for sympathy known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' signals the sound-alike: the plea 'pity us', said out loud, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Piteous means deserving pity, describing someone in a wretched, pathetic condition.

clue.text: Reverse decision for transplant?

definitions.meaning: a reversal of one's opinion or decision
literally, a heart transplant changes the heart

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a reversal is just a transplant.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading: a transplant is literally a change of heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a change of mind; the literal reading names organ replacement surgery.

clue.text: Jokes about RI volunteers and prudes

indicators.note: about means the jokes go around the other letters

parts.note: puns are jokes based on words' double senses
RI is religious instruction, kept as written
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Jokes about religious instruction and volunteers are made by prudes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a container signal, not 'concerning'. RI is religious instruction in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritans, in the general sense, are people with strict moral views, so prudes.

clue.text: Irritable as spirit diluted

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits such as whisky
tempered means moderated or diluted

explanation.surface: Someone is grumpy because their spirits have been watered down.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'short' is a small serving of spirits, as against beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-tempered means quick to anger, a synonym for irritable.

clue.text: One among many to get lift

indicators.note: among means the one is placed amid the many, inside them

parts.note: a host is a great many
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One person in a crowd hopes to be given a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts I inside HOST.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist is to raise up, so it means lift as a verb.

clue.text: Quiet time that hurt one easily convinced

parts.note: soft means quiet
ouch is what someone says when something hurt

explanation.surface: A quiet moment of pain afflicts a gullible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft touch is someone easily persuaded or imposed upon, an idiom.

clue.text: Mourn rate worked out for dividend

indicators.note: worked out here means the letters of mourn rate are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grieves over a rate of return calculated for a shareholder's dividend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dividend' suggests shares, but in arithmetic it is the number being divided.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fraction the numerator is the number being divided, which mathematicians call the dividend.

clue.text: Coppice material may be pinker after being pollarded

indicators.note: pollarding cuts a tree back at the top, so the first letter is lopped off

parts.note: rosier means pinker

explanation.surface: Wood from a coppice could turn a deeper pink once the trees are cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after being pollarded' removes the head of ROSIER, its R. Pollarding is cutting a tree back to its trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Osier is willow grown in coppices for its pliable rods, used in basketry.

clue.text: Move quickly in rejection of old English currency once

indicators.note: in means the quick movement goes inside the other letters
rejection means turning back, so old English's letters are read backwards

parts.note: to scud is to move fast, as clouds do

explanation.surface: Someone moves fast to reject an old English coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejection of' turns OE into EO; 'in' is the container signal. 'old English currency' is a false grouping.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was the currency of Portugal before the euro, so a former currency.

clue.text: Bread that's asked for at checkout?

definitions.text: Bread that's asked for at checkout?

parts.words: Bread that's asked for at checkout?
parts.note: bread is slang for money; at a shop till you can ask for money to be handed back to you along with your purchase

explanation.surface: A shopper asks for a loaf at the supermarket till.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' suggests a loaf, but it is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashback is money a customer withdraws from their account at a shop's till.

clue.text: Perhaps Liverpool player with time must accept brilliant winger

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the player and time hold the other letters

parts.note: Liverpool FC players are nicknamed the Reds; perhaps marks this as an example
a star is a brilliant performer

explanation.surface: A Liverpool footballer, given time, must welcome a brilliant wide player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must accept' is the container signal. 'winger' looks like football but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird, and a winger is a crossword word for a bird.

clue.text: In some ways, a lemon is sweet

indicators.note: ways here means arrangements, so the letters of a lemon is are put in another order

explanation.surface: A sour fruit like a lemon is, oddly, rather sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In some ways' rearranges A LEMON IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina pudding is a traditional British dessert, and a sweet means a pudding.

clue.text: Angle moderates rejected is something to be savoured

parts.note: to fish is to angle

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the moderates' letters are read backwards

parts.note: wets is British slang for moderate members of the Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone's angle that moderates have been rejected is relished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns WETS into STEW. 'Wets' were the moderate Tories who opposed Thatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish stew is a dish, something eaten with relish.

clue.text: Get rid of Nero — at heart a fiddler

parts.note: to scrap is to get rid of

indicators.note: at heart means the central letters of Nero are taken

explanation.surface: Getting rid of Emperor Nero, who was famously a fiddler at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' takes ER from nERo. Nero supposedly fiddled while Rome burned.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor violinist is said to scrape away at the instrument, so a scraper is a fiddler.

clue.text: Mother's party going west for medical application

indicators.note: going west in an across answer means read right to left, backwards

parts.note: ma is mother, so mother's gives MAS
Lab is the abbreviation for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: Mother's political party moves west seeking medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns MAS plus LAB backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is a soothing resin-based ointment applied to the skin.

clue.text: Do posers put these on fashionable transport?

parts.note: pretentious people put on airs
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: Poseurs wonder whether to wear these when using trendy transport.
explanation.definitionFit: An airship is a powered lighter-than-air craft, a means of transport.

clue.text: The last of this readily available drink

indicators.note: the last of picks the final letter of this

parts.note: handy means readily available

explanation.surface: The last of this easily obtainable drink is offered.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade or ginger beer, a popular British drink.

clue.text: One smoulders as people in club must lose protection

indicators.note: the outer letters protect the word, so losing them removes its ends

parts.note: members are people in a club

explanation.surface: Club members must give up their protection while someone smoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must lose protection' strips the ends M and S from MEMBERS.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a glowing piece of coal or wood that smoulders in a dying fire.

clue.text: White Rose represented in a different way

indicators.note: re-presented, presented anew, means the letters of white rose are shown in a new order

explanation.surface: The White Rose of Yorkshire is depicted differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges WHITE ROSE. The white rose is the emblem of Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means differently or in another manner, a synonym.

clue.text: Short picture — origin of only adult version

indicators.note: short means the picture word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: an image is a picture

indicators.note: origin means the beginning, the first letter of only

explanation.surface: A brief image from the source of the only adult edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' turns IMAGE into IMAG; 'origin of' adds O from only.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final, adult stage of an insect after metamorphosis.

clue.text: First class requirement of a radio

definitions.meaning: in English primary schools, ... is the first class children join
a radio needs good ... of signals to work

explanation.surface: A top-quality radio needs certain specifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First class' looks like 'top quality', but it is the first school year: in England 'reception' is the class for four-to-five-year-olds.
explanation.definitionFit: Reception names both the starting class of primary school and the receiving of broadcast signals.

clue.text: Almost perfect place to pull

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one short, losing its last letter

parts.note: heaven is the perfect place

explanation.surface: A nearly ideal spot to tug on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts N from HEAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to haul or pull with great effort, a synonym.

clue.text: Sponge, say, or exotic food cooked here?

indicators.note: exotic means strange or outlandish, so the letters of sponge say or are made strange by rearranging

explanation.surface: Asking whether sponge cake or something foreign is cooked in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges SPONGE SAY OR. A greasy spoon is British slang for a cheap, basic café serving fried food.
explanation.definitionFit: A greasy spoon is a cheap café where fried meals are prepared, so a place food is cooked.
